global_assumptions: Universe is the positive integers with its usual order. Every candidate language is infinite. The indexed family X={L_1,L_2,...} is countable and fully accessible to both players.
The author explicitly gives both players a membership oracle taking (x,i) and deciding x∈L_i.

An unknown target K=L_i* is fixed. At each positive round the adversary announces an element of K, then the generator announces one positive integer. Every element of K must eventually occur in the adversary stream. Repetitions are not explicitly forbidden in this edition.
Unless a setting changes this explicitly, the generator is deterministic and the adversary may depend on previous outputs.
Eventual validity means there exists a play-dependent finite t0 such that every output from t0 onward lies in K and is new relative to both players. No uniform or computable t0 is specified.
earlier-supplied-manuscript.criticality: Recursive: a consistent L_i is critical exactly when it is contained in every earlier critical language. The first critical language is the least-indexed consistent language.
earlier-supplied-manuscript.access_and_effectivity: The membership oracle is explicit, but criticality uses exact inclusion between infinite languages. The cited descriptions do not supply an effective reduction of those inclusion tests to membership queries, or a time bound. The mathematical guarantees are semantic under the described language access.

arxiv-2608-01320-v1.locations: Section 2, printed 7–8 / PDF 9–10; Section 3.1, printed 10–12 / PDF 12–14.
global_assumptions: Universe is the positive integers; all candidate languages are infinite. The indexed countable family L={L_1,L_2,...} is fully accessible to both players. The cited model does not specify a representation or an explicit membership-oracle interface.

The adversary fixes K=L_i* and announces an element of K before the generator responds with one positive integer each round. Every element of K must occur at some finite adversary round. This edition does not explicitly prohibit repeated adversary values.
The default generator is deterministic and the adversary may be adaptive.
Eventual validity requires a finite, adversary-dependent threshold after which every output is in K and has not previously been announced by either player.
arxiv-2608-01320-v1.criticality: All-earlier-consistent: L_i is critical iff it is consistent and L_i⊆L_j for every consistent j<i. This is the literal v1 Definition 3.2, independently confirmed in the same-version author HTML.
arxiv-2608-01320-v1.access_and_effectivity: The family is fully accessible, and algorithms use exact inclusion/criticality. No effective presentation, computable convergence bound, or running-time bound is part of the cited theorem context. Semantic guarantees must be kept distinct from an implementation using a specified finite interface.

arxiv-2608-01320-v2.locations: Section 2, printed 6–8 / PDF 8–10; Section 3.1, printed 9–12 / PDF 11–14.
global_assumptions: Universe is the positive integers. All candidate languages are infinite. The countable indexed family L={L_1,L_2,...} is fully accessible to both players. The cited model does not specify an effective representation or explicit membership-oracle interface.

An unknown K=L_i★ is chosen. Each round the adversary announces one element of K, then the generator responds with one positive integer. The adversary must announce every element of K exactly once: this edition explicitly requires enumeration without repetition.
The generator is deterministic and the adversary may be adaptive unless a later setting says otherwise.
Eventual validity means a finite play-dependent threshold after which all outputs are in K and new relative to either player. No effective threshold is asserted.
arxiv-2608-01320-v2.criticality: Recursive: begin with the least-indexed consistent language; thereafter a consistent L_i is critical iff it is contained in every earlier critical L_j. The footnote and Remark 3.7 explicitly distinguish this from the all-earlier-consistent definition.
arxiv-2608-01320-v2.access_and_effectivity: Algorithms use semantic exact inclusion and critical-chain updates under full access to the language family. The cited statements do not claim a computable implementation from membership queries alone or any complexity bound.

shared_definitions.ownership_density: A is the set of values whose first announcement belongs to the adversary; D is the set whose first announcement belongs to the generator. The adversary moves first each round. μ_n(S)=|S∩{1,...,n}|. Under full enumeration, A and D∩K partition K. The density is liminf_n μ_n(D∩K)/μ_n(K). Infinite K makes the denominator eventually positive and unbounded.
shared_definitions.consistency_scope_focus: Consistency at a round means containing every adversary value observed so far, including the current announcement when updated. The scope of size s is the first s candidate indices. The focus is the highest-indexed critical language in that scope.
shared_definitions.switch_loss: An adversary value is a switch loss when it is outside the focus at the end of the preceding round. Its arrival falsifies that old focus. Being a switch loss does not itself require first ownership by the adversary; charging bounds restrict to previously unannounced losses.
shared_definitions.patient_schedule: Start s_0=1 and τ=1. Retain scope between rounds. After an adversary announcement update consistency and criticality. Falsification invokes backtracking and increments τ. Otherwise, after 2^τ preceding steps with unchanged focus, expand scope by one; increment τ if that expansion changes focus. Output the least integer in the resulting focus not announced by either player. Backtracking, when no consistent language is in scope, expands to find one; otherwise truncate to the greatest old critical index still critical, or the least consistent index if no old critical one survives.
shared_definitions.target_normalization: After eventual focus containment in K is established, the density proofs identify the ordered target with the positive integers by target rank. In that analysis [n] denotes the first n target elements; finitely many early announcements are absorbed in a fixed constant. This is an analysis normalization, not knowledge of K given to the generator.
shared_definitions.partial_closure: Partial enumeration replaces coverage of K by coverage of an infinite K′⊆K; K′ need not be a candidate. Density remains relative to K. The transformed family lists intersections over nonempty finite sets I of original indices, in binary indicator order: code(I)=Σ_{i∈I}2^(i−1), and L′_I=⋂_{i∈I}L_i. The source discards finite intersections, or assumes all displayed transformed languages infinite for exposition.
shared_definitions.random_density: The adversary is oblivious: its deterministic target enumeration is fixed before the generator random choices. Randomness is in independent uniform permutations of finite blocks/groups. Density is liminf_n E[μ_n(D∩K)]/μ_n(K); the expectation is inside the liminf. This is an expected coverage guarantee, not an asserted almost-sure density theorem.
shared_definitions.blocks: A reserved integer lies in one of the disjoint finite blocks. W contains integers neither announced by either player nor reserved. A newly announced unreserved adversary integer triggers a new block; associate it with that block, giving C_r=B_r plus its trigger when present. Completeness under an order concerns inclusion of a block or its designated initial head in the target prefix.
shared_definitions.multi_order_v1: Fix a positive finite k and k permutations σ_i of the positive integers, interpreted as element-to-rank maps: [n]_i=σ_i^(-1)({1,...,n}). Set μ_i,n(S)=|S∩[n]_i|. Deterministic density is min_i liminf_n μ_i,n(D∩K)/μ_i,n(K); randomized density puts E around the numerator inside each liminf. The same generator serves every order.
shared_definitions.multi_order_v2: Fix a positive finite k and k bijections σ_i of the positive integers, interpreted as rank-to-element enumerations: [n]_i=σ_i({1,...,n}). Set μ_i,n(S)=|S∩[n]_i|. The guarantee is min_i of the target-relative liminf, with expectation in each numerator for the randomized setting. A single generator serves all k orders.
shared_definitions.auxiliary_tools: The block arguments use f(m)=1−(1−1/(m+1))^m from Ranking for online matching, with f(m)→1−1/e, and finite low-crossing partitions into groups of size s, with crossing count ≤4(m/s)^(1−1/k). The latter construction is proved in the edition’s Appendix A.

items.mathematical_claim: Start s_0=1 and τ=1. Retain scope between rounds. After an adversary announcement update consistency and criticality. Falsification invokes backtracking and increments τ. Otherwise, after 2^τ preceding steps with unchanged focus, expand scope by one; increment τ if that expansion changes focus. Output the least integer in the resulting focus not announced by either player. Backtracking, when no consistent language is in scope, expands to find one; otherwise truncate to the greatest old critical index still critical, or the least consistent index if no old critical one survives.
